transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marc (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Lisa (NorthStar Head of Security), Raj (NorthStar Platform), Oliver (NorthStar PM)

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving out time for the weekly POC security sync. Quick readout — we'll cover SSO, audit logs and retention, SOC2 docs, and any KMS/encryption Qs. Marc will walk through the SAML test plan.

[00:22] Lisa (NorthStar): Thanks. We got a couple of security reviewers looped in but this sync is fine. Biggest asks from my side: we need SOC2 evidence, clarity on who owns keys and whether we can get audit logs into our S3, and SSO that maps to our groups for RBAC.

[00:40] Marc (Redwood SE): Cool. Quick recap: for the pilot we're running Redwood hosted tenant, with audit-log export enabled to an S3 bucket you provide; SSO via SAML with group mapping so your IDP groups map to RBAC roles; and we support customer-managed KMS for encrypting at-rest keys — we can discuss HSM integration if you need FIPS/HSM later on.

[01:05] Raj (NorthStar): Quick Q on the KMS bit — when you say customer-managed KMS, do you mean Redwood can be configured to use our AWS KMS CMKs, or you provide a separate KMS? We can't have plaintext keys that we don't control.

[01:18] Marc (Redwood SE): Yes, we can configure Redwood to use your AWS KMS CMK for the data-at-rest envelope keys. There is a small ops step to rotate and authorize the key. For HSM you suggested earlier, that would be a roadmap item and we'd need enterprise package; for the pilot we typically do customer-managed KMS via AWS.

[01:40] Lisa: Ok good — that addresses a primary blocker. Next, audit logs: what fields are in the logs and can we route them to our S3 in near-real-time? We need at least request id, user id, model id, latency, and full token counts, plus, ideally, request payload redaction options.

[02:05] Marc: The audit logs contain request/response metadata — timestamps, request id, user id, route, model variant, latencies, and an obfuscated payload by default. For the POC we can include a configurable log mode: minimal (no payload), metadata-only, or expanded with pseudonymized payload. We'll share the logs schema in the doc bundle. For export, we stream to your S3 via Kinesis Firehose or direct put depending on your preference.

[02:40] Oliver (NorthStar PM): Does the streaming add latency to inference? We need to make sure benchmarks aren't affected.

[02:50] Marc: No, export is asynchronous; it doesn't add to the user request path. The only overhead is telemetry generation which is negligible.

[03:05] Aisha: Great. On SOC 2, we have a Type II report and recent pen test summary. I'll share redacted artifacts and the security page link after the call. Lisa, will redaction be ok for your team or do you need raw artifacts?

[03:20] Lisa: Redacted SOC2 is fine to start; we may need to see some test evidence later, but initial redacted is sufficient for procurement. Also need a contact for incident response and SLA details.

[03:35] Sofia (CSM): I can own the incident response contact — I'll include the SOC and incident response contact in the email.

[03:48] Raj: About retention — our legal wants 90 days for audit logs for the pilot, but we originally said 30. Can Redwood support 90 days? Also want to confirm deletion procedures after pilot.

[04:05] Marc: Yes, retention is configurable. For hosted we can retain in your S3 for any window you want; Redwood's default retention is 30 days but we can set the export and lifecycle to 90 for your bucket and then perform a final purge when the pilot ends. We'll add the retention and deletion steps to the runbook.

[04:30] Lisa: And what about GDPR/data residency? We need logs kept in us-east-1 for now.

[04:38] Marc: No problem — we can configure the export region to match S3 bucket region (us-east-1). For the inference itself, hosting region is in us-east-1 as well for the pilot.

[04:55] Oliver: On SSO mapping: can we enforce SCIM group sync or is it just SAML attributes?

[05:03] Marc: Currently we support SAML with group attributes and we have a SCIM sync in beta. For the pilot we'll do SAML group mapping; if you need SCIM for automated provisioning we'll plan that in the next phase.

[05:18] Lisa: Ok, SAML group mapping is fine for now but we want the ability to map to our internal roles.

[05:25] Marc: We'll include a sample mapping table and test cases — e.g., IDP group "payments-admin" -> Redwood role "admin", "payments-dev" -> "developer". We'll also include acceptance tests for mapping.

[05:40] Aisha: Quick note on encryption in transit: we use TLS 1.2+ and mTLS options for private deployments. For hosted we can offer connection restrictions and IP allowlists too.

[05:54] Raj: mTLS would be nice but might be heavy for the pilot; IP allowlist plus SSO is ok. But we do want proof of TLS ciphers and cert rotation schedule.

[06:10] Marc: We'll include cipher suite info and cert rotation cadence in the doc bundle.

[06:20] Lisa: About pen test evidence — redacted screenshots and executive summary are usually enough. If we need raw logs, we will request formally.

[06:32] Aisha: Ok I'll send the SOC2 and pen test summary after the call.

[06:40] Oliver: On success criteria: earlier we said 99th percentile latency < 300ms for single-turn prompts under the pilot traffic. Are we still aligned?

[06:50] Marc: That was the target; in our staging runs we saw 99p around 220-260ms for the model variant you've picked, so should be achievable. We'll run a formal benchmark next week with your traffic profile.

[07:05] Raj: For the benchmark we need to ensure the dataset doesn't contain PII; we can provide synthetic traffic. Also we want to measure token billing accuracy — request vs billed tokens.

[07:18] Marc: We'll include token accounting in the benchmark. We can export per-request token counts and cross-check with billing logs.

[07:30] Lisa: One more on audit logs: retention for logs that include pseudonymized payloads — do you offer automated redaction or is it on our side?

[07:40] Marc: We offer both: configurable server-side redaction for certain fields and a pseudonymization option. If you want full redaction of payloads, choose metadata-only mode. We'll show sample outputs.

[07:58] Aisha: Let's walk through the SAML test flow. Marc?

[08:03] Marc: Sure. Step 1: we provide SAML SP metadata and sample assertion consumer URL. Step 2: you configure your IdP with the metadata and send us a test SAML response for a test user. Step 3: we validate group attributes and map to roles. Step 4: run acceptance tests to ensure login, role-based access, and token issuance. I'll send a detailed checklist.

[08:30] Lisa: Do you support IdP-initiated SSO or only SP-initiated? We use both depending on tool.

[08:38] Marc: We support both. We'll include endpoints for each and example flows.

[08:46] Oliver: Any manual steps for us to enable group attribute release? Some IdPs require admin consent.

[08:54] Lisa: We'll have to get our IdP admin to release group attributes — I've added that to the action items.

[09:03] Aisha: Quick compliance Q from procurement: what's the SLA during pilot and how do incidents escalate?

[09:12] Sofia: For pilots we provide best-effort support; we can outline a basic incident response with 24-hour initial acknowledgment and escalation to SE if needed. If you need guaranteed SLAs we can discuss dedicated capacity and a paid SLA.

[09:28] Raj: Fine for pilot. For dedicated later we may need 1-hour P1.

[09:35] Aisha: Noted. We'll document escalation path.

[09:40] Lisa: Could you also confirm log ingestion format (JSON line, gzipped) and whether we can get compressed batched deliveries?

[09:51] Marc: Yes — logs are newline-delimited JSON by default; we can batch and gzip via Firehose. We'll include schema and examples.

[10:05] Oliver: On deletion — do you offer a certificate or attestation once data is purged at pilot end? Legal often asks for confirmation.

[10:18] Marc: We can provide a deletion attestation stating object keys removed and a retention runbook. We'll record the lifecycle steps.

[10:30] Lisa: Good — that will keep legal happy.

[10:36] Aisha: Anything else?

[10:40] Lisa: One last small ask: can you provide a brief mapping of Redwood roles to our internal roles for the pilot so our security team can validate RBAC?

[10:50] Marc: Yes, sample mapping will be in the SAML doc.

[11:00] Aisha: Great. Recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2 + pen test summary and security links; Marc will send SAML metadata, test checklist, and logs schema; Raj to provide S3 ARN and retention reqs; we schedule benchmark for next Tuesday in the proposed window.

[11:20] Raj: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the bucket and sample traffic by Monday.

[11:28] Oliver: Thanks everyone.

[11:30] Aisha: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with artifacts and calendar invite for the benchmark.

Meeting end.
